note: Generated by scripts/gen-gallery.mjs. Each card is one preview page joined to the selection guidance of the family it imports from. Family-level guidance appears only on that family's canonical documentation route, never on a supplemental page.

cards.title: Accordion
cards.summary: Bounded sections that open one at a time, or several. Height is transitioned rather than keyframed, so an interrupted open reverses from where it actually is.
cards.chooseWhen: Several titled sections share one column and the reader opens them one at a time.
cards.avoidWhen: Only one section can collapse, or the panel is a disclosure attached to a control.

cards.title: Action menu & buttons
cards.summary: Commands as data. One ActionDefinition array collapses behind a trigger (ActionMenu), spreads out as buttons (ActionButtons), or both at once — the first few as buttons and the rest in an overflow menu — so a toolbar and its overflow can never offer different things.
cards.chooseWhen: A row, card or header offers the same set of actions repeatedly and the overflow must collapse consistently.
cards.avoidWhen: You are building a bespoke menu anatomy, or the trigger is a right-click.

cards.title: Action overlays
cards.summary: A dialog, a sheet, and a confirmation with their footers generated. The primitives own the surface; these own the part every screen otherwise rebuilds — two buttons in a fixed order, and a confirm that knows about async work and forms.
cards.chooseWhen: Any application modal — dialog, sheet or confirmation — including its async confirm lifecycle.
cards.avoidWhen: The panel is non-modal and anchored to its trigger.

cards.title: Actions
cards.summary: One typed action definition, rendered by every surface that shows actions — a page toolbar, a card menu, a table row, the command palette — with the confirm, the loading state, and the errors owned in one place.
cards.chooseWhen: The same operation runs from a table row, a card menu and the command palette, and all three must get one confirm, one loading state and one error path.
cards.avoidWhen: One surface owns the action and nothing else invokes it — a registry then adds indirection for a single caller.

cards.title: Activities
cards.summary: What happened to a record, and who did it. ActivityFeed is the timeline of events; ActivityLog is the mixed one — events and comments on the same rail, with a composer. A headline is typed segments rather than a sentence, so the actor, the field, and the status each render as themselves.
cards.chooseWhen: An audit or activity log renders actor, change and time, grouped by day.
cards.avoidWhen: The entries are milestones or a changelog, or the thread is a discussion.

cards.title: AI chat
cards.summary: A transcript and the twelve surfaces it is built from. There is no fetcher, no router and no streaming client here: messages, the input, the queue and the staged files are all props, and submitting is a callback — because every provider streams differently and every app stores a conversation differently.
cards.chooseWhen: A conversational surface streams assistant messages, tool calls, artifacts and attachments.
cards.avoidWhen: The thread is human discussion on a record, or the input is a single prompt field.

cards.title: Alert
cards.summary: A message about something that just happened. The tint and the border carry the tone; only the icon is coloured, so the text stays legible in both themes.
cards.chooseWhen: A region reports its own state — informational alert, empty, loading, error, or progress.
cards.avoidWhen: The placeholder should mimic the eventual layout, or the message is transient.

cards.title: Alert dialog
cards.summary: The one modal surface in the kit, and the only page about it. Dialog, alert dialog and sheet are not separate components: each is this surface with some of its settings filled in and a name that says why. DialogContent is OverlayContent with placement=“center”. AlertDialogContent is a centred surface that nothing dismisses but an answer, given with AlertDialogAction or AlertDialogCancel. SheetContent is OverlayContent at an edge. Those are the parts that set something; the root, trigger, close, body, title and description around them are always Overlay's own. Learn the settings once here; use a preset when its name says what you mean, and configure OverlayContent for a combination no preset names.
cards.chooseWhen: Documenting or extending the alert-dialog anatomy itself inside base.
cards.avoidWhen: You are confirming a destructive action in an app — that lifecycle, focus trap and async state belong to ConfirmDialog.

cards.title: Analytics
cards.summary: Every metric surface in the kit, on one data shape. A figure written as MetricData renders in a strip, a grid, a hero card or a comparison without being remapped — so the formatting, the trend inference and the empty case are decided once instead of at each call site.
cards.chooseWhen: Figures are summarised — metric tiles, trends, comparisons, a heatmap or a titled chart card.
cards.avoidWhen: You are rendering the chart itself with no framing.

cards.title: App shell
cards.summary: The outermost layout a signed-in product lives in: a collapsing navigation column with the page in the inset beside it, or a stacked shell with the navigation across the top.
cards.chooseWhen: The application needs its outermost frame — a sidebar with an inset, a stacked header over content, or a topbar with a collapsible rail beneath it.
cards.avoidWhen: You are inside a shell already and want a region of the page: a titled section, a width constraint, or a two-column split.

cards.title: Aspect ratio
cards.summary: A frame that keeps its proportion as its width changes — a cover image, a video, a map tile. Reach for it whenever media has to hold its shape before it loads, so the page does not jump when it arrives.
cards.chooseWhen: A media box must hold a fixed ratio while its width is decided by the layout.
cards.avoidWhen: The element already has intrinsic dimensions, or you want a square avatar.

cards.title: Async combobox
cards.summary: One family at two levels. The pickers are what most fields want — ResourceCombobox and SuggestionsCombobox fetch for you, AsyncCombobox and AsyncMultiCombobox take results you already hold — and all four run on one engine: a debounced query, a minimum length, a status row, grouping, an inline create, scroll pagination and an apply footer. Underneath is the Base UI anatomy with the kit's field surface applied; drop to the parts when no picker fits.
cards.chooseWhen: Options arrive from a fetch, the field selects application resources, or it proposes completions as the user types.
cards.avoidWhen: The options are a small in-memory list, you are composing a bespoke anatomy, or a trigger character inserts entities into text.

cards.title: Async preview
cards.summary: A popover that fetches when it opens. The kit owns the surface, the trigger, the four states, and the three things that make hover-fetching hard to get right — aborting, racing, and refetching what it already has. The consumer owns the request and what a record looks like.
cards.chooseWhen: A trigger fetches its content when it opens, and needs loading, empty and error states.
cards.avoidWhen: The content is already loaded, or the surface is modal.

cards.title: Auth shells
cards.summary: A welcoming entry to your application: a brand, a focused form, useful links, and an optional story alongside it. Compose the page with AuthShell, or arrange your own AuthCard and AuthSplitPanel. Your application owns the form and its flow.
cards.chooseWhen: Sign-in, registration and recovery pages share a centred card and optional split panel.
cards.avoidWhen: The page sits inside the authenticated shell.

cards.title: Avatar
cards.summary: A person or an entity, as an image with an initials fallback. StackedAvatars is the overlapping row with an overflow count.
cards.chooseWhen: Showing a person or entity as an image with an initials fallback, alone or stacked.
cards.avoidWhen: The image is content rather than identity, or you need an upload affordance.

cards.title: Badge
cards.summary: A short status mark. It takes a tone, like everything else that carries colour in the kit, and can draw its own status dot so meaning does not rest on hue alone.
cards.chooseWhen: A short status or count sits beside the thing it describes and carries a semantic tone.
cards.avoidWhen: The text is a full sentence, or the tone is decoration rather than state.

cards.title: Batch action bar
cards.summary: The bar that appears once a selection exists. A count, the bulk actions, and a way out — shared by every surface that can select more than one thing.
cards.chooseWhen: A multi-select produces a selection whose actions must appear without shifting the list.
cards.avoidWhen: Actions apply to one row, or the surface is a page-level form.

cards.title: Breadcrumbs
cards.summary: The trail to the current page. Separators are aria-hidden, so it is not announced as “Home slash Orders slash”.
cards.chooseWhen: Moving between sibling views or pages — tabs, breadcrumbs, pagination, page heading.
cards.avoidWhen: The destinations are application shell regions, or the tabs are saved data views.

cards.title: Button
cards.summary: The action primitive. Presentation splits along two independent axes: tone is semantic colour intent, buttonStyle is fill treatment.
cards.chooseWhen: Any activation control — including one that carries a loading state, a tooltip, or sits in a group.
cards.avoidWhen: The control navigates and should be an anchor, or it toggles a persistent state.

cards.title: Calendar
cards.summary: The grid on its own, for a page that shows a month rather than asking for a date. Built on date-fns, not a calendar library.
cards.chooseWhen: The user picks a date, range, month or time from a calendar surface.
cards.avoidWhen: The date is typed as text, or you are only displaying a date.

cards.title: Card
cards.summary: The single surface primitive. Every framed region in the kit is one — if Card does not expose the chrome you need, extend it rather than introducing a second card.
cards.chooseWhen: A surface needs visible chrome — border, padding, header and footer regions.
cards.avoidWhen: You are framing reusable content that the call site should frame instead, or the rows are a list.

cards.title: Carousel
cards.summary: A horizontal or vertical track the reader pages through. It is native CSS scroll-snap with controls on top, not a JS-driven slider.
cards.chooseWhen: Peer items exceed the width and horizontal paging is the intended reading order.
cards.avoidWhen: All items should be visible at once, or the overflow is a tab strip.

cards.title: Catalogue & partners
cards.summary: Product search appearance, stock management, supplier profiles, and booking details. Structured for everyday catalogue operations.

cards.title: Chart
cards.summary: Recharts with the kit's tooltip, legend, and colour wiring. The container maps each data key to a token, so a chart follows the theme with no per-theme configuration.
cards.chooseWhen: Rendering a Recharts chart that must inherit the kit's tokens, legend and tooltip chrome.
cards.avoidWhen: The number is a single figure with a trend, or the chart needs a titled card frame.

cards.title: Checkbox
cards.summary: A box that is checked, unchecked, or indeterminate. The check and the dash are Lucide icons, not hand-drawn paths — a bespoke polyline is a second icon vocabulary in a kit that already has one.

cards.title: Collapsible
cards.summary: One region that opens and closes. Where Accordion manages a set of sections, Collapsible is a single disclosure with no siblings to coordinate.

cards.title: Color input
cards.summary: A colour value with a swatch. It accepts any CSS colour, including a token that resolves to one, and hands the picker’s choice back in whichever notation your tokens are written in — oklch, hex, rgb or hsl.
cards.chooseWhen: A single typed value needs a specialised editor — colour, datetime, phone, slider or tags.
cards.avoidWhen: The value is plain text or a number with a unit.

cards.title: Combobox
cards.summary: One family at two levels. The pickers are what most fields want — ResourceCombobox and SuggestionsCombobox fetch for you, AsyncCombobox and AsyncMultiCombobox take results you already hold — and all four run on one engine: a debounced query, a minimum length, a status row, grouping, an inline create, scroll pagination and an apply footer. Underneath is the Base UI anatomy with the kit's field surface applied; drop to the parts when no picker fits.
cards.chooseWhen: Composing a filtered single- or multi-select from its parts, with options already in memory.
cards.avoidWhen: Options arrive from a fetch, or you want the assembled control rather than the anatomy.

cards.title: Command
cards.summary: The command palette. A filtered list over an input, either inline or in a dialog bound to a shortcut.
cards.chooseWhen: A keyboard-first palette lists commands across groups, usually behind a shortcut.
cards.avoidWhen: The palette searches application records rather than commands.

cards.title: Comments
cards.summary: A thread attached to any record. The composer, the timeline, and the states between them — replying, editing, submitting, failed. It owns none of the fetching: every control appears because there is a callback for it, so a button that does nothing cannot exist.
cards.chooseWhen: People discuss a record in a thread, with a composer and attachments.
cards.avoidWhen: The entries are system-generated, or the conversation is with an assistant.

cards.title: Commerce
cards.summary: Reusable blocks for checkout, fulfillment, billing, and customer accounts. Each adapts to its container and keeps application actions in consumer callbacks.
cards.chooseWhen: Admin screens present orders, invoices, carts, fulfilment and loyalty.
cards.avoidWhen: The record is a catalogue product, whose options and readiness live in features/products.

cards.title: Contact: email, phone & URL
cards.summary: A contact detail as the anchor that acts on it — mailto for an email, tel for a phone number, href for a URL. All three are built on Link and share one rule: the text can be shortened or regrouped for a reader, and the target is always built from the full value, never from the text.

cards.title: Containers
cards.summary: The four blocks a page is assembled from. One responsibility each — scroll, measure, rhythm, columns — so a page never grows two scroll containers or two content widths.
cards.chooseWhen: A page region needs width constraint, a titled section, or a two-column split.
cards.avoidWhen: The children are peers needing only spacing, or the region is the app shell.

cards.title: Content block & icon badge
cards.summary: ContentBlock is a titled region that is NOT a Card — a labelled group inside one — and it owns the four surfaces a region can take. IconBadge is the kit's glyph-in-a-medallion, the mark that sits at the head of one. DateBlock has a page of its own.

cards.title: Context menu
cards.summary: The composable menu underneath ActionMenu, opened from a trigger or by right-click. Reach for it when the definition-driven ActionMenu cannot express the menu you need — a submenu, a radio group, a custom row. The context menu reuses these rows wholesale, so it lives here.
cards.chooseWhen: The trigger is a right-click on a region that has its own actions.
cards.avoidWhen: The trigger is a visible button, or the actions repeat across rows.

cards.title: Copyable
cards.summary: A value with a copy button. It confirms in place and raises a toast, because a copy that gives no feedback is indistinguishable from one that failed.
cards.chooseWhen: A value exists to be copied — an id, key, or reference — and needs copy feedback.
cards.avoidWhen: The value is prose, or the copy affordance belongs to a whole block.

cards.title: Currency input
cards.summary: An amount and its currency, kept in separate channels so neither has to be parsed back out of a formatted string.

cards.title: Data table
cards.summary: One table at two levels. DataView is the complete resource index — search, saved views, filters, table controls and result navigation in one surface — and it is what most index screens want. DataTable is the engine it renders: a TanStack table where TanStack owns the row model and this owns the toolbar, sticky panes, full screen, selection bar, pager and empty state. Reach for DataTable directly when there is nothing to search or filter.
cards.chooseWhen: A table needs columns, sorting, selection, cell renderers and a toolbar.
cards.avoidWhen: The dataset needs several saved views, or you are writing table markup directly.

cards.title: Data view & data table
cards.summary: One table at two levels. DataView is the complete resource index — search, saved views, filters, table controls and result navigation in one surface — and it is what most index screens want. DataTable is the engine it renders: a TanStack table where TanStack owns the row model and this owns the toolbar, sticky panes, full screen, selection bar, pager and empty state. Reach for DataTable directly when there is nothing to search or filter.
cards.chooseWhen: One dataset is presented through switchable views with saved tabs, a toolbar and pagination.
cards.avoidWhen: There is one table and no view switching, or you need the table body alone.

cards.title: Date block
cards.summary: A date set as a date: a leaf with the month across its top and the day as its subject, for a row whose subject is WHEN something happens — an agenda, a booking, an event. Everywhere else a date is a value, and the date primitives format it inline.

cards.title: Date picker
cards.summary: A day, a range, or several days, behind a field that wears the same surface as every other control.

cards.title: Dates & times
cards.summary: A moment, the span between two, how long ago one was, and how long something took. Every date primitive goes through one parse and takes its date-fns locale from the provider’s dates config, so one setting translates all of them. Duration sits beside them as a length rather than a moment — no calendar, no timezone, no daylight saving — which is why it is a separate component.

cards.title: Decimal input
cards.summary: A number with a fixed number of decimal places. A text input, not type=number — see the note below.

cards.title: Dialog
cards.summary: The one modal surface in the kit, and the only page about it. Dialog, alert dialog and sheet are not separate components: each is this surface with some of its settings filled in and a name that says why. DialogContent is OverlayContent with placement=“center”. AlertDialogContent is a centred surface that nothing dismisses but an answer, given with AlertDialogAction or AlertDialogCancel. SheetContent is OverlayContent at an edge. Those are the parts that set something; the root, trigger, close, body, title and description around them are always Overlay's own. Learn the settings once here; use a preset when its name says what you mean, and configure OverlayContent for a combination no preset names.
cards.chooseWhen: Documenting or extending the dialog anatomy itself inside base.
cards.avoidWhen: You are presenting a modal in an app — the portal, focus trap, scroll lock and async confirm lifecycle belong to features/overlays.

cards.title: Dropdown & context menu
cards.summary: The composable menu underneath ActionMenu, opened from a trigger or by right-click. Reach for it when the definition-driven ActionMenu cannot express the menu you need — a submenu, a radio group, a custom row. The context menu reuses these rows wholesale, so it lives here.
cards.chooseWhen: Composing a menu anatomy — submenus, radio and checkbox items — from its parts.
cards.avoidWhen: You want the assembled row-actions control, or the trigger is a right-click.

cards.title: Empty state
cards.summary: What to show when there is nothing to show. It names the absence and offers the next step — an empty state that only explains is a dead end.

cards.title: Event calendar
cards.summary: A month grid, a week strip, or an agenda over one list of events. The view decides only the range of days and how they are laid out — placing events onto days is the same code every time, so switching view can never move an event.
cards.chooseWhen: Events are placed on a calendar the user navigates by period.
cards.avoidWhen: The user is picking a date, or the sequence is chronological rather than spatial.

cards.title: Filters
cards.summary: A controlled filter bar. Every value is a string array, because a filter's real home is the URL and a URL has only strings — one shape means one serialiser, one parser, and a filter set that survives a shared link.
cards.chooseWhen: Users build predicates over fields, with operators, editors and pills.
cards.avoidWhen: Filtering is one search box, or the choices are fixed tabs.

cards.title: Form binding
cards.summary: The headless contract between a form library and the kit's fields. One small interface — useField — that plain React state, react-hook-form, or anything else can satisfy.
cards.chooseWhen: Binding a field to state you already own, without a form library.
cards.avoidWhen: React Hook Form owns the state, or the fields come from a schema.

cards.title: Form field
cards.summary: The label, the supporting line, and the error, wired to whatever control sits inside. One supporting line, not three stacked hints.

cards.title: Form workflow
cards.summary: The parts a form needs around its fields: a titled section, the action bar at its foot, the summary that appears when submission fails, the banner that appears when it has unsaved work, and the submit button that says what it is doing. Beside them, the two states a region shows instead of content — loading and failed.
cards.chooseWhen: Assembling a form's visible structure — label, control, support text, sections and an actions bar.
cards.avoidWhen: The fields come from a schema, or you only need the binding hooks.

cards.title: Global search
cards.summary: The command palette: one list across people, bookings, invoices, and files, walked with the arrow keys. It does not search — the query is controlled and the results are given, because debounce, endpoint, ranking, and permissions all belong to the app. What it owns is the part every palette shares.
cards.chooseWhen: One search surface spans record types, with tabs, idle and empty states.
cards.avoidWhen: The palette lists commands, or the search scopes one collection.

cards.title: Header
cards.summary: The shell's top bar. Slot-driven for its contents and fixed in its arrangement — which is the half every hand-built header gets wrong the first time a search field and an account menu share a row.
cards.chooseWhen: The application header carries breadcrumbs, search, notifications and the user menu.
cards.avoidWhen: The heading names a page rather than the application.

cards.title: Hover card
cards.summary: A preview that opens while the pointer rests on a name or a link — a person, an order, a page — so a reader can glance at it without leaving where they are. It is an accelerator, never a route: everything in it has to be one click away as well, because hover does not exist on touch.
cards.chooseWhen: Hovering a reference reveals a preview the reader does not have to act on.
cards.avoidWhen: The content is essential, interactive, or must be reachable by keyboard alone.

cards.title: Inline stat
cards.summary: One label and one value — the pair that sits inside another surface's chrome: a card footer, a header strip, a row of totals. A set of facts about one thing is a MetadataList instead.

cards.title: Input
cards.summary: The text field, and the shared surface every control in the kit wears — same height, border, focus ring, invalid state, and disabled treatment. SearchInput and PasswordInput are this field with an affordance pre-wired, so they live here too.
cards.chooseWhen: Free text is typed — plain, multiline, password, search or slug.
cards.avoidWhen: The value is numeric with a unit, or picked from a set.

cards.title: Input group
cards.summary: A bordered shell that owns the focus ring on behalf of whichever control sits inside it, so the control is stripped of its own chrome and the two never draw a box each. For a field that needs something attached to it — a unit, a prefix, an action — rather than beside it.
cards.chooseWhen: A control needs an affix inside its border — an icon, unit, prefix button or counter.
cards.avoidWhen: The affix is a separate field, or the label belongs above the control.

cards.title: Item
cards.summary: The row primitive that lists, menus, and tables compose. Media, content, and actions, with the media aligning to the first line whenever a description is present.
cards.chooseWhen: A row carries identity — media, title, description and trailing actions — in a list or a menu.
cards.avoidWhen: The row is tabular data with aligned columns, or the surface needs card chrome.

cards.title: Kanban & sync
cards.summary: A drag-and-drop board over dnd-kit, and the dialog body for a “reconcile the last N hours” run. The board translates dnd-kit's “id A was dropped over id B” into “this item moved from column X position 2 to column Y position 0” — which is the part every board has to write.
cards.chooseWhen: Records move between columns by dragging, and the board owns that state.
cards.avoidWhen: The columns are read-only, or ordering is a table sort.

cards.title: Keyboard key
cards.summary: A key cap for a shortcut written into the interface — a palette hint, a menu accelerator, a line of help. It is the browser's own kbd element underneath, so the meaning survives for a screen reader and in plain text without the styling.

cards.title: Label
cards.summary: The text that names a control. Usually reached through FormField rather than directly — but it is here for a control the kit does not ship.
cards.chooseWhen: Naming a form control so the label and control are associated.
cards.avoidWhen: The text is a heading, a static field name, or a value's caption.

cards.title: Map
cards.summary: A Leaflet surface composed the way the rest of the kit is: layers, markers, and controls are components, and the ones that belong to a control register themselves with it. Leaflet and its plugins are optional peers, loaded only when a map actually mounts.
cards.chooseWhen: Geographic data is displayed or drawn, including markers, shapes and draw controls.
cards.avoidWhen: The location is a single coordinate value to read or type.

cards.title: Measures: quantity, dimensions & file size
cards.summary: A number and the unit it is counted or measured in: a quantity of things, a physical measure, a size in two or three dimensions, a size in bytes. Each keeps the number apart from the unit until render, so the part that goes wrong by hand — the plural, the unit’s abbreviation, the multiplication sign, which megabyte — is decided in one place.

cards.title: Media library
cards.summary: The asset browser: search, filter, sort, select, edit, upload. Every field is read through an accessor, because nobody's asset records look like ours — they come from S3, Cloudinary, a media collection, a CMS, each with its own field names.
cards.chooseWhen: Existing assets are browsed, previewed, searched and picked.
cards.avoidWhen: The user is contributing new files, or one image is being replaced.

cards.title: Mentions
cards.summary: Inline references to domain records, embedded in rich text. A trigger character per kind opens the picker; picking one writes an atomic chip into the body and registers the reference alongside it. Comments and activities are both built on this.
cards.chooseWhen: Typing a trigger character suggests entities and inserts them as chips.
cards.avoidWhen: The field selects one resource up front, or the suggestions are commands.

cards.title: Menubar
cards.summary: The menu bar of a desktop application, for an editor or a workspace with more commands than a toolbar can show. The bar and its triggers come from here; the menus themselves are the dropdown menu's, imported from base/dropdown-menu beside it.
cards.chooseWhen: An application-style menu bar sits persistently across the top of a workspace.
cards.avoidWhen: The menu hangs off a single button, or the bar is site navigation.

cards.title: Metadata list
cards.summary: Label/value facts about one thing, in three layouts. A fact is data with a kind, not a node — writing { kind: 'money', value: 48200, currency: 'USD' } hands the amount to the primitive that knows the currency's exponent and the locale's separators. A single pair inside another surface is an InlineStat.

cards.title: Money
cards.summary: An amount and its currency, formatted for a locale — and optionally beside a converted second value. Never a number formatted by hand: a currency has a position, a separator, and a decimal count that all differ by locale.

cards.title: Names & initials
cards.summary: A person’s name, normalised for display, and the initials derived from it. They share a page because they read the same value: Initials is computed from the name rather than stored beside it, so an avatar and the label next to it cannot disagree.

cards.title: Navigation menu
cards.summary: A horizontal bar whose entries open a panel of links — the mega-menu of a marketing header, a product switcher, a section whose children are worth previewing. It does not know which route is current, so an application's own navigation belongs in SideNav, NavigationTabs or AppSidebar.
cards.chooseWhen: Site navigation needs grouped panels of links under top-level triggers.
cards.avoidWhen: The items are commands rather than destinations, or the shell owns the navigation.

cards.title: Numbers, ranges & ratios
cards.summary: A number on its own, a span between two, and a value against the total it is measured out of. All five render tabular figures, so they can share a column and still align; they stay separate components because each carries something a bare number drops — the range’s locale dash, the ratio’s total, the rating’s scale.

cards.title: One-time code input
cards.summary: The field for a short code sent by text message or email, drawn one box per character so the reader can check it against the message at a glance. It stays a single input underneath, which is what lets paste and SMS autofill fill every box at once.
cards.chooseWhen: A one-time code is entered as separate character cells.
cards.avoidWhen: The code is pasted as one string into an ordinary field.

cards.title: Options & variants
cards.summary: The options a customer chooses between, and the sellable combinations they generate. Two surfaces that belong together: adding a value changes the variant grid, and a reader who cannot see both while doing it is guessing at what they just made. Everything on this page is live — add an option, name it, give it values, then generate.

cards.title: Order
cards.summary: An order is not one list of goods with one status. It splits into fulfillment groups, each with its own state and location, and its money moves on an axis of its own — which is why an order can be Refunded and Unfulfilled at the same time.

cards.title: Overlay
cards.summary: The one modal surface in the kit, and the only page about it. Dialog, alert dialog and sheet are not separate components: each is this surface with some of its settings filled in and a name that says why. DialogContent is OverlayContent with placement=“center”. AlertDialogContent is a centred surface that nothing dismisses but an answer, given with AlertDialogAction or AlertDialogCancel. SheetContent is OverlayContent at an edge. Those are the parts that set something; the root, trigger, close, body, title and description around them are always Overlay's own. Learn the settings once here; use a preset when its name says what you mean, and configure OverlayContent for a combination no preset names.
cards.chooseWhen: Building a new modal surface inside the kit that must share the dialog/sheet anatomy.
cards.avoidWhen: You are consuming the kit — application modals come from features/overlays.

cards.title: Page, page header, page actions
cards.summary: The block every screen opens with, the routed version of it, and the actions beside it. Three components because a heading is also used on its own — inside a drawer, above a step, at the top of a card — and because how many actions become buttons is a decision, not a rendering.
cards.chooseWhen: A page needs its title, description and primary actions in the standard arrangement.
cards.avoidWhen: The page is a record's index or show view with a fuller shell.

cards.title: Pagination
cards.summary: Page numbers with ellipses. The range is computed by paginationRange, which is exported so a custom control can use the same arithmetic.

cards.title: Percentage input
cards.summary: A percentage, with the sign as a suffix on the field rather than a character in the value.

cards.title: Phone input
cards.summary: A dial code and a number, in two channels, so the country prefix is never parsed back out of the digits.

cards.title: Places: address & coordinates
cards.summary: A location, in the two forms a product stores one: a postal address and a latitude–longitude pair. Each is shaped by the place rather than the reader — an address takes its country’s line order, not the reader’s language, and a coordinate keeps only the decimals that still mean a distance.
cards.chooseWhen: Displaying or formatting exactly one read-only value — currency/money, date, email, file size, initials — with no interaction.
cards.avoidWhen: The value is editable, or the text is prose in a typographic role.

cards.title: Popover
cards.summary: A panel anchored to a trigger. Not a modal: the page stays live behind it, focus is not trapped, and dismissing it costs a click outside. For a decision the reader must answer, that is a dialog; for a name on hover, that is a tooltip. This is the one in between — a filter, a settings pane, a definition worth reading.
cards.chooseWhen: A non-modal panel is anchored to a trigger and may hold interactive content.
cards.avoidWhen: The panel is a list of actions, or it must trap focus and block the page.

cards.title: Popover menu
cards.summary: A Popover holding a Command: trigger → header band → search → list → footer band. It picks a VALUE from a searchable list hung off any button — who owns this, which project, what status — where ActionMenu behind the same kind of trigger runs commands instead. It is not a form control: no field surface, no name, no form value. For those, the field IS the control — see Select and Combobox.
cards.chooseWhen: A popover's content is a simple list of actions and does not need the full menu anatomy.
cards.avoidWhen: Items need submenus, checkboxes or radios, or the actions repeat across rows.

cards.title: Product surfaces
cards.summary: What a product page is assembled from: what is ready to publish, what the product is made of, what it is sold under, and the price it adds up to. Every value is a ReactNode, because a price, a stock level and an SKU are already formatted by the app that owns them — this family arranges them and never tries to format money.
cards.chooseWhen: Presenting catalogue records — options, readiness, policies and quotes — in the admin profile.
cards.avoidWhen: The record is an order, invoice or shipment.

cards.title: Progress
cards.summary: A determinate bar when the total is known, and a travelling band when it is not. The indeterminate form drops its ARIA value attributes rather than reporting a number it does not have. ProgressCircle is the same measurement drawn as a ring, for the places where the reading has to sit inside the mark.

cards.title: QR code
cards.summary: A scannable symbol drawn in the theme's own colours, as SVG so it scales and prints without blurring.
cards.chooseWhen: A value must be scannable on screen or in print.
cards.avoidWhen: The value only needs copying to the clipboard rather than scanning off the screen.

cards.title: Radio groups
cards.summary: One choice from a visible set, in four shapes: plain radios, cards for a choice the reader is weighing, a list for options whose second line is the decision, and pills for a compact switch. Every one is a radio group — one tab stop, arrows move between options.
cards.chooseWhen: The user picks from a known, closed set — checkbox, radio, switch or select.
cards.avoidWhen: The set is large enough to need filtering, or the values are free text.

cards.title: Repeater
cards.summary: A list the reader edits row by row — add, remove, reorder. The generic Repeater renders any row you give it; the three specialised ones cover the shapes that come up constantly.
cards.chooseWhen: A field holds a variable-length list the user adds to, reorders or removes from.
cards.avoidWhen: The list length is fixed, or the shape comes from a schema.

cards.title: Resizable panels
cards.summary: Split panes the reader drags apart — a document beside its inspector, a list beside its detail. Reach for it when the reader, not the layout, knows how much room each side deserves; a split nobody needs to move is a Grid.
cards.chooseWhen: The user sets the split between panes and the size should persist.
cards.avoidWhen: The split is fixed by the layout, or the region is a page shell.

cards.title: Resource assignment
cards.summary: The “this record has a venue assigned; here it is, and here is how to change it” panel. The card owns the shape — a panel, a dialog, a pending choice, and a confirm that waits for the write. The picker inside the dialog is yours, because every assignment is a different search.
cards.chooseWhen: A resource is shared with or assigned to principals through a dialog.
cards.avoidWhen: You are displaying permissions rather than changing them.

cards.title: Resource shells
cards.summary: The skeleton every list and detail screen shares: a header identifying the thing, a toolbar, a body, sometimes an aside, and the three states that replace the body while it waits, fails, or comes back empty. The shells own that; the table, the form, and the fetch stay the screen's.
cards.chooseWhen: A record's index or show page needs its standard shell — header, actions bar and sections.
cards.avoidWhen: The page is a workspace shell, or the content is one table.

cards.title: Rich text editor
cards.summary: A TipTap editor with formatting, undo and redo, HTML source mode, and composition slots. The imperative handle supports inserting content and replacing mention triggers at the caret.
cards.chooseWhen: Users author formatted content with a toolbar and counts.
cards.avoidWhen: The input is plain multiline text, or the content is only displayed.

cards.title: Schema form
cards.summary: A form described as data: fields with a type, a label, and the rules that govern them. Every control is already a kit component, so what this owns is the mapping — which control a type gets, how sections bucket fields, and when a message appears.
cards.chooseWhen: Fields are generated from a schema at runtime rather than written by hand.
cards.avoidWhen: The form is known at build time, or you only need field structure.

cards.title: Scroll area
cards.summary: A bounded scroll region, plus the two small primitives that keep meaning available without showing it: BooleanIndicator and VisuallyHidden.
cards.chooseWhen: Presenting label/key and value facts, a collapsible region, a keyboard hint or a scrollable pane.
cards.avoidWhen: The pair is an editable field, or the row carries identity and actions.

cards.title: Select
cards.summary: A single choice from a list too long to show at once. Its rows use the shared menu row, so it matches every other menu surface in the kit.

cards.title: Separator
cards.summary: A rule between regions. Decorative by default, so assistive technology does not announce a line that carries no meaning.

cards.title: Settings shell
cards.summary: The two navigations that sit beside content rather than above it — the rail between the pages of one section, and the table of contents within one page — and AsideNavShell, which is the rail composed beside a column of content, as a settings area is.
cards.chooseWhen: Settings pages share an aside navigation beside their content.
cards.avoidWhen: The navigation is the application sidebar, or the sections are tabs.

cards.title: Sheet
cards.summary: The one modal surface in the kit, and the only page about it. Dialog, alert dialog and sheet are not separate components: each is this surface with some of its settings filled in and a name that says why. DialogContent is OverlayContent with placement=“center”. AlertDialogContent is a centred surface that nothing dismisses but an answer, given with AlertDialogAction or AlertDialogCancel. SheetContent is OverlayContent at an edge. Those are the parts that set something; the root, trigger, close, body, title and description around them are always Overlay's own. Learn the settings once here; use a preset when its name says what you mean, and configure OverlayContent for a combination no preset names.
cards.chooseWhen: Documenting the sheet anatomy, or inside base where features/overlays cannot be imported.
cards.avoidWhen: You are presenting an edge-anchored modal in an app.

cards.title: Side nav, section nav & settings shell
cards.summary: The two navigations that sit beside content rather than above it — the rail between the pages of one section, and the table of contents within one page — and AsideNavShell, which is the rail composed beside a column of content, as a settings area is.
cards.chooseWhen: The shell's own navigation — side, section or category — positions destinations.
cards.avoidWhen: The user moves between sibling views inside one page.

cards.title: Sidebar
cards.summary: The navigation panel and the page beside it. A provider holds the open state so a trigger anywhere on the page can reach it, the panel collapses to icons or off-canvas, and the inset is the document's main landmark. base/sidebar is the primitive; layout/app-shell assembles it into a shell.
cards.chooseWhen: Composing a collapsible sidebar from its parts, including the mobile presentation.
cards.avoidWhen: You want the assembled application sidebar with logo, user and workspace slots.

cards.title: Skeleton
cards.summary: A placeholder in the shape of what is loading. The composed skeletons mirror the layouts the kit already ships, so a loading page is the same geometry as the loaded one.
cards.chooseWhen: A placeholder should hold the eventual layout's shape while data loads.
cards.avoidWhen: The wait is indeterminate and unstructured, or the region failed.

cards.title: Slider
cards.summary: A value picked along a track, for a quantity the reader adjusts by feel rather than types.

cards.title: Slug field
cards.summary: A URL slug derived from another field. Accents fold, punctuation collapses, and the prefix is chrome rather than part of the value.

cards.title: Spinner
cards.summary: Indeterminate activity, as a ring with one transparent quarter. One element rather than an SVG, and it reads as motion at any size.
cards.chooseWhen: A wait is short and has no layout to preview.
cards.avoidWhen: The eventual shape is known, or the wait blocks a whole region.

cards.title: Stack & Grid
cards.summary: Stack, Grid, GridCell, AdaptiveGrid, Split, and Bleed. Every prop takes a value or a per-breakpoint object, so a layout that changes shape does not need two rendered trees.
cards.chooseWhen: Passive siblings need consistent spacing, a grid, or a stack — with no semantics of their own.
cards.avoidWhen: The children form a titled page region, or the arrangement carries meaning.

cards.title: Switch & toggle field
cards.summary: An immediate on/off state — it takes effect when flipped, with no save step — on its own, as a settings row (ToggleField), and as a feature card (SwitchCard). The row and the card are one component at two weights.

cards.title: Table
cards.summary: Rows and columns, as plain table elements. The scroll container is the only wrapper — everything else is the semantics the browser already gives you.
cards.chooseWhen: Writing table markup directly, with rows you control and no sorting or selection.
cards.avoidWhen: The table needs columns, sorting, selection or a toolbar.

cards.title: Tabs
cards.summary: A tab set following the WAI-ARIA pattern: arrows move between tabs, Home and End jump to the ends, and only the selected tab is in the tab sequence.

cards.title: Tags input
cards.summary: A list of short strings entered inline as chips. Enter commits, Backspace on an empty field removes the last one.

cards.title: Textarea
cards.summary: Multi-line text on the same field surface as Input, with the same invalid and disabled treatment.

cards.title: Time picker
cards.summary: A time of day, and the combined date-and-time field built from it.

cards.title: Timeline
cards.summary: An ordered run of events on one rail. The shared geometry under every dated list in the kit — a changelog, a set of milestones, an order's progress — so the dot, the connector and the title block are decided once rather than redrawn per caller.
cards.chooseWhen: Composing a generic vertical sequence of dated entries.
cards.avoidWhen: The sequence is a changelog, milestones or a step tracker.

cards.title: Timelines, onboarding & admin
cards.summary: Domain presentation assembled from the layers below it. The three timeline surfaces map a vocabulary onto base/timeline rather than redrawing the rail, and nothing here fetches, navigates, or confirms a destructive action — every one takes callbacks and slots.
cards.chooseWhen: A sequence is presented as changelog entries, milestones, or a step tracker.
cards.avoidWhen: The entries are a system audit log, or the sequence is a calendar.

cards.title: Toast
cards.summary: A transient notice raised from anywhere, including outside React. The queue lives in a module store, not in a provider, so a fetch handler can raise one without a hook.
cards.chooseWhen: A message is transient, non-blocking, and reports the outcome of an action.
cards.avoidWhen: The message belongs to a region, or the user must act on it.

cards.title: Toggle
cards.summary: A button that stays pressed. Not a switch and not a checkbox — it reports aria-pressed, which is the distinction spelled out in the accessibility tree.
cards.chooseWhen: A control holds a pressed state, alone or as one of a mutually exclusive group.
cards.avoidWhen: The state is a form value that submits, or the control performs an action.

cards.title: Toolbar
cards.summary: A named set of related controls with one tab stop. Tab enters or leaves the set; arrow keys move within it according to orientation.
cards.chooseWhen: A persistent group of related actions or controls needs one tab stop and arrow-key navigation.
cards.avoidWhen: The actions open from a trigger, select one value, or navigate between pages.

cards.title: Tooltip
cards.summary: A short explanation on hover and on focus. It is never the only place a piece of information lives — a tooltip is unreachable on touch and gone the moment the pointer moves.
cards.chooseWhen: A short, non-essential hint labels a control on hover or focus.
cards.avoidWhen: The content is interactive, long, or required to understand the control.

cards.title: Typography
cards.summary: Text, Heading, DisplayLabel, and TextLink. Every library-owned string reaches the DOM through one of these, so a raw element never carries type styling.
cards.chooseWhen: Rendering library-owned copy in a role — heading, body, label, link or sanitized rich text.
cards.avoidWhen: The text is a formatted data value rather than prose.

cards.title: UIRoot & UIScope
cards.summary: One component used to do both jobs, and they have different contracts. At the top of an application it owned the DOCUMENT — <body> sits above anything it renders, and a page canvas that stays light while its contents go dark is not a theme. Nested, it owned a REGION and had no business touching the document. Which one you got was inferred from whether a provider happened to be above you.
cards.chooseWhen: Setting display defaults, theme, density and scale for the app or a subtree.
cards.avoidWhen: The value is per-feature policy or domain data, which stays a prop.

cards.title: Unit inputs
cards.summary: Weight, dimensions, and coordinates: three fields whose value is a number plus a unit or a second number. Each keeps its parts in separate channels.
cards.chooseWhen: A numeric field carries a unit, currency or precision the input itself must enforce.
cards.avoidWhen: The number is plain, or it is being displayed rather than edited.

cards.title: Upload
cards.summary: Choosing files, one image, and files on their way — one family. A dropzone and a picker, an image picker that previews in its final shape, and progress for transfers the caller runs. Nothing here transfers anything: the value is File objects, and sending them is the caller's business.
cards.chooseWhen: The user contributes files — dropzone, avatar, image, or a tray with progress.
cards.avoidWhen: Existing assets are being browsed and picked rather than added.

cards.title: Value & lists
cards.summary: The two primitives for plain text rather than a typed value. Value renders one string and knows what an absent one looks like; InlineList joins several into one phrase, with the conjunction and commas the locale decides.

cards.title: Workspace record header
cards.summary: The header of a record you are working ON — an invoice, a customer, a deployment. Built on PageHeading for the title row, but not a page title: a page heading names a screen, and this identifies a thing and carries the apparatus that comes with one — media, a status, metadata.
cards.chooseWhen: The whole authenticated shell — sidebar, header and content — is assembled at once.
cards.avoidWhen: You are placing one region, or the page is unauthenticated.
